title: Open immersions descend along qcqs affine-transition limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $X_{i_0},Y_{i_0}$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to Y_{i_0}$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Write $f_i$ and $f$ for its base changes to $S_i$ and $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], there is $i\geq i_0$ such that $f_j$ is an open immersion for every $j\geq i$. No affineness of $X_{i_0}$ or $Y_{i_0}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0EUU, label lemma-descend-open-immersion, in Situation situation-descent-property; persistence by base change of open immersions

proof.text: The limit morphism $f$ is étale and a monomorphism, since it is an open immersion. These are properties of the entire morphism, with no affineness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0EUU, lemma-descend-open-immersion; open-immersion étaleness and monicity

proof.text: Check the locally finite type hypothesis needed for monomorphism descent. For every affine open $V\subseteq Y_{i_0}$, the affine basis supplies an affine cover $U_\alpha$ of $f_{i_0}^{-1}(V)$. The affine-pair finite-presentation lemma gives $\mathcal O_X(U_\alpha)=\mathcal O_Y(V)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ as algebras. The images of the finitely many $t_r$ generate this algebra. Thus this cover satisfies exactly the definition of locally finite type.

source.place: Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize; finite presentation implies finite generation

proof.text: Apply étale descent to the original $S_{i_0}$-morphism: $S_{i_0},X_{i_0},Y_{i_0}$ are qcqs, transition morphisms are affine, the limit map is étale by step 1, and the original map is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. Obtain $a\geq i_0$ with $f_a$ étale. Independently apply monomorphism descent to the same original morphism, using step 2 for locally finite type and step 1 for monicity at the limit. Obtain $b\geq i_0$ with $f_b$ monic.

Choose $i\geq a,b$ by directedness. For $c=a$ or $c=b$, write $s_c:S_i\to S_c$ for the transition. The fibre-product universal property identifies $X_i$ with $X_c\times_{Y_c}Y_i$: on maps from any scheme $T$, send the compatible pair $(x_0,t)$, with $x_0:T\to X_{i_0}$ and $t:T\to S_i$, to $((x_0,s_ct),(f_{i_0}x_0,t))$. Conversely a pair $((x_0,t_c),(y_0,t))$ compatible over $Y_c$ satisfies $y_0=f_{i_0}x_0$ and $t_c=s_ct$; send it to $(x_0,t)$. These constructions are mutually inverse by uniqueness in the universal property and identify $f_i$ with the projection to $Y_i$. For $c=a$, étale base-change stability therefore makes $f_i$ étale. For $c=b$, if $u,v:T\to X_b\times_{Y_b}Y_i$ have the same projection to $Y_i$, their projections to $X_b$ become equal after composition with $f_b$. Monicity of $f_b$ makes those projections equal, and uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property gives $u=v$. Hence $f_i$ is also monic.

source.place: Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; elementary pullback cancellation and associativity

proof.text: For every field $K$ and maps $u,v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X_i$, the equality $f_i u=f_i v$ implies $u=v$ by monicity. Thus $f_i$ is injective on $K$-points for every field. The four-way equivalence in the radicial definition node makes $f_i$ radicial. Since it is also étale, the radicial–étale open-immersion theorem makes $f_i$ an open immersion.

Fix $j\geq i$ and write $s_i:S_j\to S_i$ for the transition. The identification $X_j\cong X_i\times_{Y_i}Y_j$ sends a compatible pair $(x_0,t)$ of maps from $T$ to $X_{i_0}$ and $S_j$ to $((x_0,s_it),(f_{i_0}x_0,t))$. A compatible pair $((x_0,t_i),(y_0,t))$ in the latter product satisfies $y_0=f_{i_0}x_0$ and $t_i=s_it$, and its inverse image is $(x_0,t)$. The universal property makes these inverse morphisms of schemes, under which $f_j$ is the projection to $Y_j$. Stability of open immersions under base change, applied to the open immersion $f_i$ of step 5, makes $f_j$ an open immersion. Since $j$ was arbitrary, this proves the all-later clause.
